description: Take the Brasilia Cathedral apart piece by piece in 3D, and read the story of Oscar Niemeyer's hyperboloid church: sixteen concrete columns reaching for heaven in the middle of a planned capital.

intro: Sixteen concrete columns curve up out of the red earth and meet forty meters in the air, and between them is nothing but glass and sky. This is Oscar Niemeyer's church for a city built from nothing.
page_title: Brasilia Cathedral: Exploded 3D Model and History | Architectural Atlas

sections.body: When Brazil decided to move its capital inland, Oscar Niemeyer was given a blank plateau and told to invent a city. For its cathedral he drew sixteen identical curved columns, calculated by structural engineer Joaquim Cardozo, rising from a 70-meter circle and bending inward until they meet 40 meters up: two hands lifted to heaven, or the crown of thorns, depending on who you ask. The foundation stone was laid on 12 September 1958; the concrete skeleton stood by 1960, but the church was not inaugurated until 31 May 1970.
sections.heading: A church for a new capital

sections.body: Niemeyer, an atheist and a communist, built one of the century's most spiritual rooms. Most of the church is underground: visitors descend a ramp beneath the reflecting pool, pass through a dark tunnel, and emerge into a 70-meter nave flooded with light through the glass. Three angels by Alfredo Ceschiatti hang over the pews on steel cables. The altar was a gift from Pope Paul VI. The Way of the Cross is by Di Cavalcanti, and the stained glass that washes everything blue and green is by Marianne Peretti, installed in 1990.
sections.heading: Heaven in concrete

sections.body: The cathedral was listed as heritage in 1967, three years before it was even inaugurated: the country recognized the masterpiece before the paint was dry. In 1987 UNESCO listed the whole of Brasilia as a World Heritage Site, and in 1988 Niemeyer received the Pritzker Prize, architecture's Nobel, at 81 the oldest recipient ever. The cathedral is the building on the postcards, the silhouette that means Brasilia.
sections.heading: Listed before it opened

sections.body: Outside, four bronze Evangelists by Ceschiatti stand guard at the entrance, and a separate bell tower holds four bells donated by Spain. Beside the church sits the ovoid baptistry dome. The ensemble is pure Niemeyer: curves where a European would draw straight lines, concrete treated not as a brutal material but as something weightless. The columns look too thin to stand. Cardozo's mathematics said they would, and sixty years later they still do.
sections.heading: The ensemble around it

sections.body:
The cathedral never needed cinema; it had the history of modern architecture. Since its inauguration it has been the single most published Brazilian building in the world, the obligatory illustration in every survey of concrete, of modernism, of Latin America, of Niemeyer.

Its cultural weight was fixed early. The 1967 heritage listing, three years before the inauguration, made it official: this was a monument while still a construction site. The 1987 UNESCO listing of Brasilia and Niemeyer's 1988 Pritzker Prize then folded the building into the canon of the century, the proof that the curves the establishment had dismissed as sculpture were architecture after all.

The building also lives a second life as a national symbol. It is on Brazilian postcards, textbooks and television idents; every presidential inauguration in Brasilia is photographed against its skyline. In 1970 it gave a military-ruled country a church that looked like the future. It still does.
sections.heading: In the cultural conversation

story_title: The story of the Brasilia Cathedral

timeline.text: The foundation stone is laid as the new capital rises on the plateau.
The concrete structure of 16 columns is completed.
The cathedral is heritage-listed, three years before its inauguration.
Brasilia is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Oscar Niemeyer receives the Pritzker Architecture Prize.
Marianne Peretti's 2,000 sq m of stained glass is installed.
